stories.title: Outrage after Meta suspends No Kings Instagram account during protests
stories.summary: The coalition leaders behind nationwide pro-democracy protests that have drawn millions of Americans to the streets in recent years were frustrated when its Instagram account was temporarily shut down during its latest demonstration on Saturday. The No Kings movement’s account went dark for several hours while protests focused on increasing early voter turnout were underway, sparking censorship fears. Meta apologized on Saturday and blamed the account’s temporary suspension on an automated action that’s triggered “when accounts post, share or comment at very high frequencies”. “Unfortunately, that automated action was clearly taken in error,” Meta spokesperson Andy Stone, wrote on X. “Everything is now working as it should and we sincerely apologize.”

stories.title: Russian oil sites ablaze as Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war. reserveStories.title: UNC-Chapel Hill strikes bargain with Trump administration to end probes
reserveStories.summary: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill on Monday struck a deal with the Trump administration to end federal investigations into its handling of alleged campus antisemitism and civil rights violations. Under the terms, the highly selective public flagship will share with the federal government years’ worth data on civil rights complaints and adopt new policies, ranging from admissions changes to student activity oversight. In exchange, the U.S. departments of Justice and Education will end more than a dozen active civil rights probes into the university. UNC-Chapel Hill did not admit wrongdoing under the agreement, and the federal government said it does not intend to dictate the "content of academic speech or curricula" at the university.
